title: Kiteboard hierarchical rail and telemetry proto
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Purpose: Prototype an alternative console navigation pattern ("kiteboard" hierarchical rail) that compresses workspace switching, surfaces rollout and cost lenses, and emits richer telemetry for SLO and user behavior analysis.

Scope: 1) IA changes to primary rail: introduce hierarchical lanes (workspace > project > route) with progressive reveal and compact mode. 2) Contextual cost and rollout badges on routes. 3) Telemetry hooks for route dwell, expand/collapse events, and quick-switch invocations. 4) Prototype in Figma + interactive clickable frames, and a lightweight React prototype in the console sandbox for qualitative testing.

Goals and success metrics: 1) Reduce median time-to-switch between workspaces by 25% in moderated task flows. 2) Expose cost-per-route and active rollouts without adding cognitive load (measured by SUS + task completion). 3) Provide event stream that enables per-route latency/cost correlations for SRE.

Design principles and constraints: 1) Maintain keyboard-first discovery (tab/arrow, quick-jump). 2) Strong accessibility: aria-expanded semantics, 4.5:1 contrast on badges, screen-reader announcements for rollouts. 3) Limited vertical real-estate for teams with 20+ projects—must support sticky search and pinning. 4) Must be implementable by engineering without a backend schema change for rollout metadata; fall back to client-side augmentation when server flag absent.

Proposed interaction patterns: - Progressive lanes: top-level workspace row shows chevrons to reveal projects; projects reveal routes. Collapse preserves last-opened state per-user. - Compact mode: replaces full labels with icons and condensed badges; tooltip + quick-preview panel for long route names. - Route badges: cost indicator (sparkline minibar), rollout badge showing % of traffic & active experiments, and an alert dot for degraded SLOs. - Quick-jump command (Cmd+K) integrates with rail state to surface prioritized routes based on recency and rollout importance.

Telemetry and events (for SRE/Product): - events emitted: kiteboard.open_workspace, lane.expand, route.select, route.preview_open, badge.hover, badge_click. - payload must include: route_id, workspace_id, timestamp, previous_route_id, client_mode (compact/expanded), and rollout_id if present. Implementation note: when server rollout metadata is missing, client should attach local-rollout-stub with source="client-fallback".

Prototype deliverables: 1) Figma clickable prototype (frames + annotated redlines). 2) Lightweight React sandbox prototype with mocked event emitter and telemetry console. 3) Test script for 6 moderated sessions and a 25-person unmoderated pilot via Maze. 4) PRD section describing developer integration points and an acceptance checklist.

Acceptance criteria: - Keyboard nav works for all lanes and route actions. - Telemetry events appear in the sandbox console with correct payload shape. - Cost badges display sample data and respect 4.5:1 contrast. - PM and SRE review sign-off recorded in comments.

Implementation trade-offs: - Full server-side rollout awareness would be ideal but risks scope creep; client augmentation reduces backend dependencies at cost of temporary inconsistencies. - Compact mode increases discoverability risk for less-familiar users; will gate behind an onboarding tooltip and optional user preference.
